*   **Domain Error:** The term $1 - v^\top \Omega_Y^{-1} v$ must be positive to prevent imaginary results in the square root [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the term $1 - v^T Omega_Y^{-1} v$ must be positive to prevent imaginary results in the square root. Source [S1] provides the formula for the skewness parameter alpha_Y in Equation (13) and Equation (15), which involves a square root of the term $1 - (A omega delta)^T Omega_Y^{-1} (A omega delta)$ (or similar substitutions). In mathematics, for the result of a square root to be real (non-imaginary), the argument inside the square root must be non-negative. Since the denominator cannot be zero (which would cause division by zero), the term inside the square root must be strictly positive. The evidence explicitly shows this term under the square root, supporting the necessity of it being positive to avoid imaginary numbers.
